messages:
acme_ops: Hey team — starting ~08:14 UTC we saw a flurry of 429s from the Dedicated pool for account acct-9b2c. Customer says they have a reserved pool but traffic spiked and the client app started getting throttles. Not sure if this is misconfigured or an actual quota hit.

acme_ops: Key details: pool_id=rp-us-west-2-42, model=gpt-4-mini, region=us-west-2, expected steady rps ~40, burst up to ~200 for 20s. Observed 429s with header `x-rate-limit-reset` present.

acme_ops: Example response headers we got: `x-rwrl-limit: 60/second`, `x-rwrl-burst-remaining: 0`, `x-rwrl-reset: 8`

maria_support: thanks — can you paste the exact curl you hit and a few raw response headers/body? also did you see any 5xx or timeouts or only 429s?

acme_ops: only 429s. curl we used:```bash
curl -i -X POST \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\" \n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" \n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-4-mini","input":"summarize...","max_tokens":512}'
```

acme_ops: We also tested a batched call that split into 10 concurrent requests (same payload) to reproduce.

maria_support: ok. sounds like we hit the per-second enforcement on the reserved pool. i'm going to pull the pool config & recent telemetry. dan_sre — can you take a look at the rp-us-west-2-42 policy? any smoothing or short-window caps?

dan_sre: i'm looking. quick note: Dedicated pools have two enforced parameters: `throughput_cap` (sustained rps) and `burst_window` (short-term cap per second/min). Customers can reserve capacity (committed) but short bursts above configured burst_window get throttled to protect node stability.

dan_sre: pulling telemetry... i see a ~12s window where inbound rps peaked at ~215 then dropped back to 45. the pool's throughput_cap=60 rps, burst_window=15s with burst_multiplier=3 => allowed short burst ~180. they exceeded that by ~20%.

acme_ops: ah — the customer expected 200 bursts to be allowed. their reserved committed baseline was misunderstood. any way to give them a quicker fallback so app doesn't 429?

maria_support: options: 1) increase pool burst_multiplier / burst_window (config change, requires ops schedule & commit) 2) enable automatic overflow routing to a lower-cost fallback pool/variant to absorb excess (we have policy: route->compatible-variant) 3) smooth client side by adding token bucket at client.

pj_billing: fyi billing: spikes that route to fallback (hosted pool) will incur on-demand usage charges. need customer approval if we bump capacity temporarily.

acme_ops: they'd prefer a non-billing-affecting quick mitigation — maybe a soft queue or backoff guidance.

dan_sre: short-term mitigation we can toggle: `client_side_rate_shaper` suggestion and increase `smoothing_window` in routing to 5s to reduce instantaneous rps spike seen by pool. that's a config change on control-plane (no infra churn). i can apply a temporary smoothing policy for acct-9b2c.

maria_support: please also share precise repro steps so we can document. acme_ops — can you run a reproducible test with a `-H "X-Debug-Trace: trace-123"` header so we can correlate request IDs?

acme_ops: will do. running 10s test now (concurrent 200 -> expecting 429). command:```bash
ab -n 200 -c 200 -T 'application/json' -p payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

acme_ops: test results: ~36% 429s, 64% 200s. attached sample response: `{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","retry_after":7}`

dan_sre: correlated traces — we see `throttle_reason=reserved_pool_burst_exceeded` and logs show per-node enforcement kicking in. here's the control-plane view snippet we used (redacted):```
# reserved-pool rp-us-west-2-42
throughput_cap: 60
burst_window_seconds: 15
burst_multiplier: 3
smoothing_window_seconds: 1
# effective short burst allowance = throughput_cap * burst_multiplier = 180
```

dan_sre: because smoothing_window_seconds=1 the telemetry shows the full spike as instantaneous. increasing smoothing_window_seconds to 5 spreads it across 5s allowing bursts to be absorbed without raising total commit.

maria_support: dan — can you try a controlled change to smoothing for this acct and monitor for 10m? i'll hold on customer comms until we confirm. pj — you'll need to sign off on any billing-impact change.

pj_billing: ok to approve non-billing smoothing change as it's a routing/config tweak and doesn't spin up new nodes. if we later route to hosted fallback we'll need a purchase order.

dan_sre: applied smoothing_window_seconds=5 for acct-9b2c on rp-us-west-2-42 at 1934568001. monitoring now.

deploy-bot: [deploy] config update applied to control-plane: rp-us-west-2-42 smoothing_window_seconds=5 (change id cfg-7129).

acme_ops: retesting after ~30s... running same ab test.

acme_ops: new results: ~6% 429s, 94% 200s. headers now show `x-rwrl-burst-remaining: 42`. this is much better. :tada:

maria_support: great. i'll summarize recommendations:
- educate customer on reserved pool semantics: committed throughput vs short-burst allowance and billing implications of fallback routing
- propose config: keep smoothing_window_seconds=5 for a short trial window 24h, optionally increase burst_multiplier to 3.5 if business needs require higher peak absorb
- add client-side best practice: exponential backoff with jitter and request pacing for large fan-outs

maria_support: acme_ops — i'll open a follow-up ticket for a permanent pool config review and include cost estimate if they want a higher sustained commit or a guaranteed larger burst.

acme_ops: thank you all. please include a note on what headers to watch for so our app can auto-backoff.

maria_support: headers to watch: `x-rwrl-limit` (sustained), `x-rwrl-burst-remaining`, `retry-after`. we'll add sample backoff snippet in the follow-up ticket.

oliver_pm: filing product-ops item to surface better default smoothing for new customer pools — many customers assume burst=committed.

maria_support: closing note: resolved for now with smoothing change; flagging for review. will update thread with final ticket id.

acme_ops: appreciated — saved the day!
